findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard permissions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on all resources ("Resource": "*") to a service account user, violating least privilege and allowing this credential to fully control EC2, S3, Lambda, and CloudWatch if compromised.

Creating a long-lived IAM access key for a service account tied to an over-privileged user creates a persistent credential that, if leaked, grants broad access; static keys are inherently riskier than short-lived roles/temporary credentials.

The encrypted_secret attribute of the access key is exposed as a Terraform output (svc_deploy_key_material), which will be stored in state and shown in CLI/plan output, risking leakage of sensitive key material to anyone with access to state files or logs.

An IAM user is created for a service/deploy purpose with force_destroy enabled and no permissions boundary, increasing the attack surface for credential misuse and making it easier to recreate/destroy the account without additional controls.
